title: What If You Stood on Pluto's Moon Charon?

scenes.text: What if you stood on Charon? A whole world would hang motionless above you.
Charon and Pluto are tidally locked, orbiting each other every 6.4 days, always showing the same faces.
So from one side of Charon, Pluto never rises or sets. From the other side, it never appears at all.
Pluto is about 2,300 kilometers wide and under 20,000 kilometers away, so it would span roughly 7 degrees, about 13 times wider than our Moon looks.
Charon is half as wide as Pluto, and the two circle a point in empty space between them.
Two worlds locked face to face, turning together once every 6.4 days.

description:
What if you stood on Charon, Pluto's largest moon?
Pluto would hang in one spot in the sky, roughly 13 times wider than our Moon looks, or you would never see it at all.
